subject: Pure data entry / data capture / keying
reason: Global Core v3.1 isolates 18 pure digital/remote rows across 17 buyers and 6 countries after removing inspection+entry and platform collisions. Historical examples explicitly specify data capture/keying, error-rate and turnaround deliverables. SPM can compress manual labor with OCR/vision/LLM plus exception QA.
next_test: Country-specific price/value and buyer recurrence analysis; live use only later.

subject: Evidence / literature synthesis and rapid/systematic reviews
reason: 29 pure digital/remote historical rows, 22 buyers, 7 countries after domain-specialist cases are separated. Workflow has highly compressible search-screen-extract-synthesize steps, while regulated/scientific domains may require credentialed final review.
next_test: Split general evidence review from PhD/regulated review and model expert-QA unit economics.

subject: Data collection / research orchestration
reason: 17 pure digital/remote rows across 16 buyers and 8 countries remain after fieldwork-heavy exclusions. Research/data collection can be orchestrated with panels, freelancers and automated processing, but some assignments may still require local or respondent access.
next_test: Decompose remote survey/panel work vs primary field collection and price panel capacity.

subject: Data validation / coding services
reason: 11 pure digital/remote rows across 7 buyers and 4 countries, with median observed bidders 3.5. The work is structurally compatible with deterministic validation, LLM-assisted coding and human exception handling.
next_test: Extract exact acceptance/error metrics and human QA ratios from historical examples.

subject: Pure data/content migration services
reason: After removing SAP/system implementations and a semantic migration collision, 11 pure digital/remote rows remain across 8 buyers and 5 countries. Real market exists but is smaller than v2 suggested and may require platform expertise.
next_test: Classify by common source-target stacks and identify freelancer/partner supply depth.

subject: USA court reporting agency/network
reason: Strict title-led v3.2 has 3,003 awards, 191 buyers and 219 suppliers. 78.5% of awards are associated with strong network-name or repeat-organization suppliers; 47 suppliers serve at least 3 buyers. QA shows repeat agencies such as VET Reporting, Gradillas Court Reporters, Capital Reporting, Anderson Court Reporting and other multi-buyer firms.
next_test: Model agency margin, certification geography and subcontractor supply; distinguish virtual vs onsite court reporting.

subject: USA sign-language interpretation network
reason: 330 strict awards across 126 buyers and 82 suppliers; 79.4% of awards map to strong-network or repeat-organization suppliers, only 7.3% individual/ambiguous, with 21 suppliers serving at least 3 buyers. Historical structure strongly supports an agency/network model.
next_test: Split onsite/remote ASL and measure network capacity, hourly pricing and certification requirements.

subject: USA general language interpretation network
reason: 928 strict awards, 268 buyers, 216 suppliers; 61.9% strong-network/repeat-org award share and 33 suppliers serve at least 3 buyers. Agency structure is empirically present, though onsite languages and rare-language fulfillment add operational complexity.
next_test: Segment phone/video/onsite and rare-language procurement economics.

subject: USA expert-witness network
reason: 7,674 strict awards across 182 buyers and 2,088 suppliers with 138 suppliers serving at least 3 buyers. Repeat firms exist, but direct individual experts remain materially important and strong-network-name share is only 0.3%; supplier top-buyer concentration can also be very high. Network economics are plausible but not proven as the dominant model.
next_test: Identify firms that explicitly intermediate experts and compare markups versus direct expert awards.

subject: Australia independent review services
reason: v3.2 isolates 91 awards, 38 buyers, 80 suppliers, median AUD 68,866.88 and top supplier share 4.4%. QA sample has 29/30 report/review/analysis cues and zero field cues; repeat winners include small review/advisory firms as well as larger consultancies. Domain-specific reviewers remain necessary for many assignments.
next_test: Segment governance/policy reviews from engineering/legal/financial peer reviews and model expert-network fulfillment.

subject: Australia policy/program evaluation
reason: After removing Defence technical Test & Evaluation, v3.2 leaves 113 remote-analytical policy/program evaluations across 22 buyers and 64 suppliers, median AUD 238,839.10, top supplier 12.4%. QA shows actual health, social, drought, mental-health and government-program evaluations won by evaluation consultancies, universities and advisory firms.
next_test: Break deliverables into desk analysis, survey/interviews, stakeholder engagement and report components; price expert/freelancer supply.

subject: Australia project/program assurance reviews
reason: 607 awards and 115 suppliers show a real repeated market, but only 19 buyers and historical QA contains cost, ICT, management-system and other specialist assurance. Strong opportunity may exist through credentialed partners rather than SPM-core delivery.
next_test: Map Department of Finance/other panel structures and supplier credentials historically, without inferring current eligibility.

subject: Australia technical Test & Evaluation
reason: Semantic QA showed Defence technical Test and Evaluation contamination inside the former PROGRAM_EVALUATION bucket. v3.2 isolates 67 technical-specialist awards across only 2 buyers. This is not evidence for a lean policy-evaluation lane.
next_test: No priority unless a qualified defence/testing partner strategy is intentionally pursued.

subject: Office consumables / toner resale
reason: Open-world broker QA finds multiple recurring office-consumable/toner clusters. One cluster has 24 records/15 buyers/10 suppliers and median value 80k native with median 5 bidders; another toner cluster has 16 records/12 buyers/8 suppliers and top supplier share 23%, while other clusters are heavily concentrated and should be avoided. Standardized SKUs make supplier arbitrage plausible, but concentration and OEM/original-toner requirements vary sharply.
next_test: Deep-dive only the fragmented toner/office-consumable cohorts; benchmark wholesale quotes and OEM-equivalent constraints.

subject: Food supply brokerage
reason: High historical volume and buyer breadth exist, but perishability, delivery frequency, food safety, locality and likely thin margins make the observed asymmetry worse than office/IT consumables.

subject: Laboratory reagents / consumables resale
reason: Historical clusters show real recurring demand and some supplier fragmentation, but compatibility, regulated medical/laboratory use, product registration and approved-brand constraints can dominate. Do not treat as generic commodity brokerage.
next_test: Separate non-medical generic lab consumables from regulated diagnostics/reagents.

subject: Global information-work v3.0 pure counts
reason: Manual semantic QA found registre/enregistrement substring collisions, inspection+entry mixtures, OCR-software procurement and embedded IT. v3.1 is the current pure-core authority with 110 pure digital/remote rows; source records remain preserved in non-pure classes.
next_test: Use v3.1 only for pure-core strategic promotion.

subject: Australia PROGRAM_EVALUATION v3.1 aggregate
reason: QA found Defence technical Test and Evaluation inside PROGRAM_EVALUATION. v3.2 separates 115 policy/program evaluation rows, 67 technical test/evaluation rows and 168 generic unresolved evaluation rows.
next_test: Use v3.2 split for all strategic interpretation.
